articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The article reports on the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) successful annual auction and swap meet held on April 4, 2004, which raised substantial funds for the club and offered a wide variety of astronomy items. It also provides a detailed calendar of SJAA activities for May and June 2004, including general meetings, ATM (Amateur Telescope Making) classes, astronomy classes, and various star parties.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: The article discusses upcoming celestial events, lamenting that a total lunar eclipse and Venus transit will be largely invisible from the author's location, though the Moon's first quarter will be viewable. It critiques existing lunar maps for being overly complex for beginners and introduces a simple, customizable moon map template to facilitate observation. The author also reviews John Westfall's "Atlas Of The Lunar Terminator," praising it as a good primer for lunar observation despite its dated images.

articles.title: Churning Whitecaps
articles.summary: This article provides advanced tips for observing Jupiter, detailing how to spot features like the turbulence around the Great Red Spot, festoons, and the equatorial band, emphasizing the importance of steady seeing and high magnification. It also offers an update on the current visibility of other planets, including Saturn, Mars, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, and Venus. A significant portion of the article is dedicated to the upcoming, rare Venus transit of the Sun, outlining its visibility zones, rarity, and necessary preparations like solar filters.

articles.title: The Glow of Creation
articles.summary: This article details an observing program focused on finding HII regions, or active star-forming areas, within external galaxies during "galaxy season." It provides specific observing notes and descriptions, often drawing from deep-sky expert Steve Gottlieb's logs, for several NGC and IC galaxies across various constellations. The author emphasizes the profound experience of visually identifying these distant "glows of creation," akin to local nebulae, using amateur telescopes.

articles.title: Editor's Semi-Dark Matter
articles.summary: This "Editor's Semi-Dark Matter" column provides several updates and requests for reader input on future articles. It announces the May 7 deadline for Project Astro applications and highlights AstroCon 2004. The editor seeks comments for articles exploring amateur astronomers' contributions to the hobby and reviews of astronomy textbooks, while also discussing format and content changes in a special PDF-only issue of the newsletter.

articles.title: Attend A Conjunction!
articles.summary: AstroCon 2004, a "once-in-a-lifetime conjunction" of four major astronomical organizations (Astronomical League, AAVSO, ALPO, and ASP), is scheduled for July 20-24, 2004, in the San Francisco Bay Area. The convention will feature sessions, professional speakers, workshops, vendors, and special events including tours of Lick Observatory and Chabot Space & Science Center, an awards banquet, and a closing banquet on the USS Hornet.

articles.title: Foothill College Astronomy Lecture Series
articles.summary: Dr. Yvonne Pendleton of NASA's Ames Research Center will deliver a non-technical, illustrated talk titled "In the Heat of the Night" as part of the Foothill College Astronomy Lecture Series. The free lecture will cover the search for infant stars, comets, and the building blocks of life, featuring new images from the Spitzer Telescope. The event will take place at Foothill College in Los Altos Hills, California, with a $2 parking fee.

articles.title: Author and Astronomer Ken Croswell to speak at the May 1st General Meeting
articles.summary: Astronomer and author Ken Croswell will be the guest speaker at the SJAA general meeting on May 1st at 8 p.m. at Houge Park. He will discuss his latest book, "Magnificent Mars," showcasing stunning images from various spacecraft to explore Mars' geology, topography, and the potential for ancient life. Croswell's books will be available for sale and autograph at the event.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article provides an update on the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, detailing the availability status of various scopes. It lists numerous telescopes immediately available for loan, scopes currently borrowed with their due dates, and those with extended loan periods, some of which are undergoing repair. SJAA members interested in borrowing a scope are instructed to contact Mike Koop, and a waiting list is maintained for popular telescopes.
